name: UPSC

levels.note: Any degree. Age 21–32 (relaxations: SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC 3 yrs). 6 attempts (General).
B.E./B.Tech in relevant branch. Age 21–30 (IES). 6 attempts.

stages.name: Preliminary Exam
stages.tests: Paper 1: GS (100 Qs, 200 marks, 2 hrs). Paper 2: CSAT (80 Qs, 200 marks, 2 hrs).
stages.note: CSAT qualifying (33%). GS score decides cut-off. Negative marking 1/3.

stages.name: Main Exam
stages.tests: 9 papers: Essay, GS I-IV, Optional I-II, Language (qualifying). Total 1750 marks.
stages.note: Written. 3 hrs per paper. Optional subject chosen by candidate.

stages.name: Personality Test (Interview)
stages.tests: 275 marks. Board of 4-5 members. 30-45 min. Personality, current affairs, optional subject.
stages.note: No coaching can substitute genuine personality. DAF (Detailed Application Form) is key.

stages.name: Final Merit
stages.tests: Mains (1750) + Interview (275) = 2025 marks. Service allocated by rank + preference.
stages.note: Top 900-1000 candidates recommended. Service allocation by merit + preference.

syllabus.pattern: 100 questions, 200 marks, 2 hours. Negative 1/3. This is the merit paper of the prelims; the cut-off is decided by the Commission each year.

topics.items: Ancient, medieval and modern Indian history, the freedom struggle, art and culture, post-independence consolidation
Physical geography of India and the world, Indian geography, economic geography, distribution of resources
Constitution, political system, panchayati raj, public policy, rights issues
Economic and social development, sustainable development, poverty, inclusion, demographics, social sector initiatives
Ecology, biodiversity, climate change, general science, current events of national and international importance

syllabus.books: UPSC Prelims Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: 80 questions, 200 marks, 2 hours. Qualifying at 33% — these marks are not counted in the merit. A low CSAT score fails candidates every year.

topics.items: Comprehension, interpersonal and communication skills, logical reasoning and analytical ability, decision making and problem solving
General mental ability, basic numeracy (Class 10 level), data interpretation (charts, graphs, tables)

syllabus.pattern: Essay 250 marks; GS I to GS IV 250 marks each; Optional Paper I and II 250 each — 1750 marks counted. English and one Indian language paper of 300 marks each are qualifying at 25%.

topics.items: Indian heritage and culture, history and geography of the world and society
Governance, constitution, polity, social justice and international relations
Technology, economic development, bio-diversity, environment, security and disaster management
Ethics, integrity and aptitude — theory plus case studies
Two essays of 125 marks each; two papers in one optional subject chosen from the UPSC list

syllabus.pattern: 275 marks. Conducted by a board on the candidate's application form, home state, education, optional subject and current affairs.

topics.items: Mental alertness, critical powers of assimilation, clear and logical exposition, balance of judgement, variety and depth of interest, leadership and social cohesion

reality: UPSC CSE is the most competitive exam in India. 10 lakh+ applicants, ~900 vacancies. Success rate < 0.1%.
Preparation takes 1-2 years minimum. Many take 3-4 attempts. Average age of successful candidate: 27-28.
Optional subject choice is crucial. Choose based on interest and scoring potential, not popularity.
Current affairs matter more than static knowledge. Read The Hindu/Indian Express daily.
Interview is not about knowledge — it tests personality, balance, and integrity. DAF preparation is key.
Service allocation: IAS > IPS > IFS > IRS (by rank). Top 100 get IAS. Rank 100-200 get IPS/IFS.

faq.q: How many attempts are allowed for UPSC CSE?
faq.a: General: 6 attempts (age 21-32). OBC: 9 attempts (age 21-35). SC/ST: unlimited (age 21-37). PwD: 9 attempts (age 21-42).

faq.q: What is the difference between IAS and IPS?
faq.a: IAS = administrative service (district collector, policy making). IPS = police service (SP, DIG, DGP). Both are Group A. IAS has higher status and broader scope.

faq.q: Can I choose my optional subject freely?
faq.a: Yes. Any subject from the UPSC list. No restriction based on graduation. Choose based on interest, syllabus overlap with GS, and availability of study material.

faq.q: What is the UPSC interview like?
faq.a: 275 marks. 4-5 member board. 30-45 minutes. Questions on DAF (hobbies, education, work), current affairs, optional subject, and situational judgment. No right/wrong answers — personality assessment.
Not mandatory. Many clear without coaching. Coaching helps with structure and mock tests. Self-study with standard books + test series is equally effective.

faq.q: Where do I find official UPSC notifications?
faq.a: upsc.gov.in (main site) and upsconline.nic.in (application). SarkariJobs+ links the official notification PDF on every listing page.

prepPlan.phase: Months 1–6 — NCERT and one book per subject
prepPlan.what: Read Class 6–12 NCERTs for history, geography, polity, economics and science, then one standard book per subject. One book read twice beats five books read once.
One newspaper a day, with a monthly compilation for revision. Write notes only for what you will revise — most aspirants write notes they never reopen.
Start Mains answer writing early, not after the prelims. Two answers a day from previous-year questions, 150 words in 7 minutes. This is the single biggest differentiator at the mains stage.
Solve 10 years of prelims papers subject-wise, then 30–40 full mocks. CSAT deserves a fixed weekly slot: 33% is a low bar but two hours of reasoning without practice is how candidates fail.
No new material. Revise your own notes, maps, current affairs compilation and error log in cycles. Give mocks at the actual slot time and keep the last week light.
